utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. We will continue with the cross-examination of Mr. Djakovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Djakovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We're grateful to you for taking the time yesterday to write out those parts of the notes which were found to be illegible. I appreciate that it took a considerable amount of your time. I'm advised that some of the passages remain illegible, which is no surprise. It happens to most of us. And you've marked these on the sheet. There are 11 pages, I understand, of your handwritten material. It's important that that is preserved. I understand one other difficulty you had, apart from deciphering some parts, was being sure about the place names in some instances and we would be grateful for just a little more assistance from you. When you finish your evidence today, we've arranged that the court deputy will give you an atlas of Kosovo to see if that assists you to identify any of the place names that you've been unable to identify so far. I'm not expecting you to spend a lot of time on that. Just see what you can do to help further, and we will be grateful for that. The cross-examination by Mr. Lukic will now continue. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Djakovic.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I see that you worked yesterday after the trial too, so today we'll keep things very short. I would just like to show you a document, the document is 6D1665. There is no translation for this document, so I'm just going to ask you to look at page 2. So could you please read something from there and give me your comments. This is a letter from the Office of the National Council for Cooperation with the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia. It was sent on the 30th of January, 2008, to our colleague Boris, who's a member of this team. So could you please slowly read out paragraph 7 of this letter. We are going to ask for it to be zoomed in. Do you see it now?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do. Paragraph 7: "The log-book of the forward command post of the command of the 3rd Army in which documents are registered starting with number 872 for the period from the 20th of March, 1999, up until the 10th of June, 1999, in spite of all the efforts made by the legal successor of the mentioned command has not been found or, rather, it has been established that the requested log-book had not been handed over and filed in the archives and also that there is no accurate information about where the log-book is and whether it was ever destroyed or lost."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd just like to ask you who this legal successor referred to here is, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Terminologically, legal successor in a way, well, it can be said it's the army command or the General Staff to which the documents were supposed to be handed over.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to where this log-book could be found, do you know?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It would be logical for it to be in the archives of the General Staff. There is no other place for it to be. The only thing I can say is that I know that there had to be a log-book because in respect of the documents that I did -- that I created at the forward command post they were logged in the log-book, including my control inspections of units on orders issued by the commander and other tasks that we carried out. You can even find out what number it was supposed to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djakovic. These were all the questions that we had for you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I wanted to request permission to be able to go into two areas --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I'll come back to you in a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There is one thing that we would like to ask just finally from our point of view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've referred a number of times, Mr. Djakovic, to the MUP staff, and that was a MUP staff for Kosovo. What was your understanding of its role?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my understanding is -- well, I haven't really given this much thought because I had direct contacts with certain persons. So I didn't really give much thought to the role of the MUP, but I think that the role of the MUP did have a certain function. My assessment is that the minister of the interior sent part of the officers from the MUP down there to reinforce the team that would practically be in charge of the work of certain secretariats of the interior in an indirect way, if I can put it that way, exercised its influence; and directly influence the overall situation in Kosovo in relation to the tasks and obligations of the police. I'm saying that because the minister of the interior, at least according to what some people said, had direct links with the secretariats and the staff of the MUP had the same kind of links with the secretariats. Down there there were, if I can put it that way, two men from the Ministry of the Interior who probably had the task to reinforce that team. I'm referring to General Djordjevic and General Obrad, Obrad Stevanovic I mean. Now, what their specific tasks were I can only - well - infer what that might be. And I've already said in a way that General Obrad Stevanovic was primarily involved with the PJPs, and as for the engagement of these units I mostly dealt with him with regard to that matter not with General Lukic. As for General Djordjevic, I did not have much in common with him except during the talks that were held and briefings; however, I as head of operations and training did not have any other contacts with General Djordjevic. I repeat again, most of my contacts were with General Obrad Stevanovic and with General Lukic's assistants or at least they introduced themselves to me as being General Lukic's assistants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What period of time are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying all of this about the period of 1998, that is to say up until the end of January, until I was there as head of operations and training. Beforehand I said that for 1999 I cannot give much reliable information because I had contacts with them very seldom because I was involved with completely different things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In your evidence initially you gave the impression that you thought that General Lukic had a very important role there, and yet you don't mention him in that context in this answer.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly, I do mention him. He was on the MUP staff and he was responsible for the work of the MUP staff. I did not say that because I believe that probably there is some documentation in relation to that. I never had any documents from the MUP except for the information that I received from the Ministry of the Interior and the state security. That is to say that I never dealt with any other documents. That's what I said yesterday to General Lukic's lawyer, when answering his questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In liaising with the MUP in relation to any actions, did you personally have direct contact with the heads of any of the seven SUPs?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The heads, no. As a matter of fact, I could only remember the name of Boro Vlahovic when I went to the commission in April because I and General Stojanovic from the MUP talked to him together. I know the others more in respect of their names. Perhaps I did see some of them individually, but I very seldom had direct contact with them. Mostly it was brigade commanders who had contact with chiefs of the secretariats of the interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, does that raise any issues for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. We did say we would give you the opportunity if anything arose in cross-examination by Defence counsel, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There was one thing from Mr. Lukic and one thing from Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yesterday Mr. Lukic asked you whether you participated in drafting the plan for combatting terrorism and you said yes. Can you tell me two things. One, what was the name of the plan? What did you call it? Was it just the plan for combatting terrorism or did it have any particular name?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That plan did not have any secret name, I know that for sure. It had no secret name, as plans do, like Grom or others that existed earlier on. So this plan did not have a name. Its name was simply the plan for combating terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija. That was its name, so to speak, in communication among us and what we were tasked to do within the command. As for its content, yesterday I pointed out, first of all, it was defence of the border; and secondly, the deblockade of roads in two stages. One stage is the deblockade of the roads behind the border belt, and the second or third is the deblockade of road throughout the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, primarily the three main roads, Kosovska Mitrovica-Rudnik-Pec; the second one Pristina-Iglarevo-Klina-Pec, and this road going through Kramovik to Djakovica. And the third road is Stimlje-Dulje-Suva Reka-Prizren. The fourth road was open, that is through Urosevac, Strpce, and Prizren. It was not blocked and no actions were planned there against the terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you said that you participated in writing the plan. Were you the only author or if there were others involved, who else was involved in writing the plan?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I've already said that I was the protagonist of the drafting, but the entire command of the corps took part, all of them who were at the command post then. That is to say that General Lazarevic on the 21 of April on orders issued by the army commander went to the forward command post with a group of officers in Djakovica, and he stayed there practically until the end of October. I think that's when this activity ended. As for the rest of the command, General Pavkovic, I as the head of the operations and teaching department and also General Lazarevic's deputy, most of the operative organs, the chiefs of arms and services subordinated to General Lazarevic, then the assistant for logistics, and the assistants to the assistant for logistics, then the chief of security and his assistants, then the assistant for moral guidance and the other organs, they were all in Pristina, at the command post there, and they took part in the elaboration of this plan proportionate to the need in terms of the information that they were supposed to provide. If you're interested in hearing who provided what elements, I can elaborate on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, that's sufficient for now. Let me then go to the other topic. Yesterday Mr. Fila asked you a couple of questions about the four civilians that attended the Joint Command meetings, and at page 26.846 he said: "Would you agree with me then that any suggestion or anything that the four said did not have any influence on what was done?" You said: "No, their influence was not really that significant." I would like to show you two documents related to that issue, the first one is P1435. I can hand you a hard copy with the help of the usher. It's dated the 22nd of September, 1998. It's from General Pavkovic, a Pristina Corps commander, to the 3rd Army command, personally to the commander General Samardzic. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In paragraph 1 we see it says: "At the meeting in Belgrade on 31 August 1998 presided over by the president of the SFRY, a plan for implementing stage five of the fight against terrorism in KiM was agreed upon." And you'll see that there was a discussion that part of that agreement was forming some new battle groups to be used in KiM. If you will go down to paragraph 4, in English we have to go to the second page. For you, General, it's at the bottom of page 1, paragraph 4 says: "During the briefing on the course of implementing stage five of the plan which was given at the meeting of the ZK for Kosovo and Metohija," and I take it that means the Joint Command? Isn't that what the ZK means there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: "At the meeting of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija on 10 September 1998, the other command organs pointed out that the VJ had not carried out two of its duties under the plan, namely, one, it had not formed rapid intervention helicopter units as the president of the FRY had ordered at the meeting on 31 August 1998; and two, two battle groups had not been moved down to KiM." My first question is: Who were the other command organs at the Joint Command meeting that are being referred to there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say that during those meetings and briefings, from what I noticed, about 20 to 25 people passed through those meetings and briefings. The fact that nobody stated at the first meeting that any kind of command was formed is true. This is definite, I'm convinced of that, otherwise I would have written it down, and it seems the most important thing to be written down had this been said. Secondly, seven or practically eight people attended the first meeting. Later some 12 to 15 persons appeared at these meetings, they were carrying out different posts and functions, including the commander of the army, the chief or the assistant commander of the 3rd Army, General Samardzic, for counter-intelligence affairs. And of course it would be in their jurisdiction in case anything was illegal --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Djakovic, let me stop you there. The VJ is obviously one command organ and the MUP is another, and what Mr. Hannis is asking is: What other command organs were involved?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are no other organs here. I don't know of any other organs. As to the role they were given, the gentleman from the republican and the federal organs, this is something that I can only speculate on or guess about and I said that yesterday. These would be the four persons referred to here plus Mr. Andreja Milosavljevic also appeared, he was there, then I think Mr. Lakovic or something like that from the state security of Pristina appeared, I think that was his surname. Then there were others, I think Mijatovic was there from the MUP. These were the people. There are no other persons. There is no other organs or persons other than the ones who were there. I don't know of any other organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I'm looking at the minutes for the meeting on the 10th of September, and those present are General Pavkovic, General Lukic, Mr. Radovic, Mr. Minic, General Stevanovic, Mr. Andjelkovic, and Mr. Sainovic. So if General Pavkovic is talking about the other command organs pointing out something at that meeting, it had to be somebody other than the VJ and the MUP, and that leaves Mr. Minic, Mr. Sainovic, and Mr. Andjelkovic, because Mr. -- or Mr. Radovic, I suppose --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any objections to what Mr. Hannis is doing. I would just like the Chamber to allow the witness to look at the records or the minutes. I apologise. Perhaps then it would be good to continue with the questioning. That is all that I wanted to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Would that help, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have no problem with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you find the entry for that date, General?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I do have an objection in the sense of the question of Mr. Hannis was it had to be somebody other than the MUP or the VJ, and I don't think the MUP is excluded as being the command that raised the issue if you look at the language in the thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but it's plural.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: MUP could very easily have raised that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I entirely accept that, Mr. Ackerman, but the language uses the plural so there must be another organ. And whether it means an organ of the Joint Command or whether it means an organ that has command responsibilities is yet another issue to be resolved. But first of all we need to identify what are the organs involved. Please continue, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's my question, General, the way I read that. When General Pavkovic from the VJ says at that September 10th meeting: "Other command organs" pointed out that the VJ hadn't done something, I assume MUP is one of the other command organ, but it's in the plural. Who else besides the MUP is he referring to there, now that you've had a chance to look at who else was attending on that day?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The remarks probably refer to, at least according to this report, to other civilians. They can refer to other civilians certain remarks, because General Pavkovic here refers to the agreement at President Milosevic's, at a meeting which was attended by the civilians that are referred to here who attended the meeting of the Joint Command. It was attended also by the army commander, by the Chief of the General Staff, and the chief of the security administration. It was also attended by President Milosevic, Stanisic probably, and any of the other organs who were present there, maybe the MUP and the army organs. So I assume this refers to their knowledge in relation to Belgrade what was agreed at a specific state level, where state, police, and army and other state organs took part, the Executive Council, the federal Executive Council, representatives of the government, so these would be the top state organs. Because these details up here are not known to me, how this functioned at the level of Belgrade, but I know for sure that the corps commander constantly went with the army commander in a helicopter to Belgrade. This is what I do know, and they went to the General Staff together. After that, they went to President Milosevic for meetings, but I don't know -- all I know about these meetings and the results is that I received an order to begin preparations based on a decision by the Supreme Council, preparations to draft a plan to deblock communications. This is all I knew --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... talking about comments that were made at the Joint Command meeting on the 10th of September, that's the meeting where he says: "The other command organs pointed out that VJ had not carried out two of its duties under the plan ..." he's not saying that happened at the meeting on the 31st of August, 1998, right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say that, but he says that the agreement is such -- the agreement in Belgrade was attended by General Samardzic too. And he refers to -- actually, he addresses General Samardzic, that he as the authorised organ, the superior organ to the corps commander, should intervene in that sense and approve the use and the formation of such a unit for rapid intervention. So he addresses the army commander in a regular procedure for it to, with his authority and force of order, implements this decision that was approved at the top levels of the state, that he then approves what is going on here with the organs of the Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You need to allow the interpretation to be complete. Mr. Fila, you wanted to say something.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to say if you show him the records from that meeting, the minutes from that meeting, I would like to see if there is a single word of that that is being claimed that Pavkovic said. I would like to find in the notes anything about any civilian stating what Mr. Hannis is putting to you. Can you please read that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I didn't have time to read this. I'm just responding to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just -- that's not the way to deal with this, Mr. Fila. If you feel that your position is somehow or other prejudiced by this further cross-examination, you should ask at the end of it for an opportunity to clarify certain matters by asking any additional questions you wish. If you feel it can't be done simply by making appropriate submissions in due course, which I suspect it can be. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, if you would go down to the bottom of the page 2 in the B/C/S of that exhibit, P1435, you'll see there's a -- "we propose," a couple of things that General Pavkovic proposes. I want you to read the sentence right above that. Can you read that out so I can ensure the translation we have is correct.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We are providing the -- moreover, we're giving the members of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija the opportunity to report to the president of the SRJ that the Army of Yugoslavia did not carry out its duties as provided under the plan."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. That's what we have on the English. Then one other document related to this topic, P1439. I have a hard copy of this one too, General. With the usher's help, I'll trade you. This is dated the 5th of October, 1998, again from General Pavkovic to the 3rd Army command addressed to the commander. Under item number 2, the second paragraph, my English translation says: "On my return from the reporting session with the ZK, Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija, on 19 and 20 September 1998, I informed you personally by telephone of the decision to form rapid intervention forces. As part of the conclusions from the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija meeting, I sent you the decision to form rapid intervention units, which you forbade in your order of 3 October." Now, would you go to the entry for the 20th of September, 1998, in the Joint Command notes you took.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's page 124 of the English, Your Honours, and in e-court, it's page 110 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, can you please give me the date on that relevant page. Is it October?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm looking for the date of the 20th of September, the meeting of 20 September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Page 121 seems to be the 19th, 123 for the 20th --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. 124 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Actually, the entry starts on 123, but the portion I want to ask about is on 124 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you find that one, General, on your B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from the 20th of September, yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I think it's the next page for you, it's Mr. Sainovic speaking. And the first thing he's recorded as saying is: "To prepare units for faster interventions ..." That's what it says, correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't know, can you read the last sentence there because it's marked as illegible here and I can't remember if that's one of the ones you went through yesterday or not.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I probably then corrected something here most likely, but then I started for Thursday, then it's crossed out, then it says "Friday the commanders of the helicopter units are to come -- unit are to come at 10.00, operative from the army."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions from what arose yesterday, Your Honour, but there was one thing. During my cross-examination of the General he had indicated that he never -- no one ever used the term Joint Command in those meetings and he never wrote that in the minutes. I didn't find the entries I was looking for while I was talking to him, but I wanted to direct the Court to page 115 and page 142 of the English. There are two entries, one where General Pavkovic says: "A body is to be formed from all the structures to take care of the realization in forming the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija beforehand," and at page 142 Mr. Sainovic is saying: "The Djakovica model is to be applied in the village of," it's an illegible word, "and in Prizren as well (meeting with the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija)." And with that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are you wanting to put these to the witness to establish --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it didn't arise from cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I think you should do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Because --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I brought it to your attention to see if you wanted to do it or if you wanted me to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please continue with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, yesterday I think you took the position that during these meetings no one used the term "Joint Command." I would ask you to look, if you can find the entry for the 8th of October, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That entry actually starts on page 141 of the English but in English I'm going to 142.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you find that, General? At the very bottom of that page you should see Mr. Sainovic speaking, and then on the next page in your B/C/S could you read that out.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "The Djakovica model should be applied to Pec and Prizren," and I put in parenthesis "(notes from a meeting of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija on the 8th of October)." This is not something that Mr. Sainovic said. I put in parenthesis that this was a meeting of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija. He didn't refer to that, I did. In my conversation with General Pavkovic, General Samardzic do refer to the Joint Command because General Samardzic also asked me about meetings of the Joint Command, and General Pavkovic and he did refer General Pavkovic to meetings of the Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... of September 1998. That starts on page 113 of the English, Your Honour, the portion I wanted to ask about is on page 115.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 15th of September, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... if you will follow to the third page, the last page for that meeting, it should be just an entry for General Pavkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We do not see the original or the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... under his name on that page.

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Plan to secure communications by secretariats." The next one: "When the plan for fortifying position is reviewed, the next, a body is to be formed of all the structures that will deal with the implementation and inform the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija beforehand."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't have any other questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just have one intervention in the transcript. I didn't want to interrupt my colleague or yourself. It is page 6 of the transcript. I believe the witness said the secret name, not the secretariat name, as it stands in the transcript. And it says: "Like Grom or others that existed later on," and in transcript it's earlier on. So that's all I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would need to put some questions arising from the questions put by Mr. Hannis. First, in relation to the minutes of the 9th of September he's being shown a letter in which General Djakovic refers to those minutes. So my question is: Is any of the civilians at that meeting on the 9th of September, 1998, the one who mentions anything that General Pavkovic says, according to that letter, and perhaps then we can see who Pavkovic is thinking of with these - how shall we put it, what can I say? - and then you can look at the 9th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is it the 10th or the 9th?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The 10th.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, yes, the 10th of September. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, well, you may put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General, sir, the Prosecutor showed you Pavkovic's letter that you are familiar with, where he talks about organs, some organs. You said one is MUP, it can be something else, I don't know, it can be state security, let's say, but it doesn't matter. There was an attempt to insinuate that the organs are actually those four civilians and that you answered me incorrectly yesterday that the civilians didn't have any influence. In your notes, is it said anywhere that those civilians said anything about the matters that Pavkovic is referring to in the letter?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't notice, but I know that as part of the -- within the command we discussed the rapid intervention forces because the circumstances required us to deal with this problem, and probably General Pavkovic, based on the agreement in Belgrade up there, reminded the army commander about the duties that were agreed on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean, am I on the right road, that Pavkovic in that sense is thinking of Belgrade and not the four civilians who are sitting with you there?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the communication I had with General Samardzic, I know that General Samardzic was informed about this proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: All right. My second question. If we were to take the suggestion that there were these civilians that, for example, these forces were formed, were these forces ever formed and did General Samardzic forbid the formation of these forces?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Samardzic did not approve the forming of these forces and this is something the Chief of the General Staff is aware of, General Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Were they ever formed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: All right. If we take the assumption stated by someone here, that General Sainovic [as interpreted] is ordering all the generals of the Army of Yugoslavia, does that mean that he could have issued an order to Samardzic to form these forces or not?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this was so, he could have done so, but he didn't even call him. I know he did not call him because the commander of the army simply did not permit the use of helicopter units in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: All right. And now to go back to what we discussed, the Prosecutor's questions of yesterday. You said yesterday that if anyone were to, anyone at these meetings - and I'm talking about the civilians, only the civilians - had some kind of proposal or suggestion or anything, and this was primarily the MUP, all of this had to go back to General Samardzic, again for approval, so they actually had no influence on implementation at all?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No direct influence at all, not according to the decisions. Nobody even tried that. I know that decisions on the use of forces, I never heard anyone tell them, Djakovic do this, do that, plan this, never. They -- only the corps commander and the army commander, at least to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: So if the commander, like you said yesterday, if the army commander ultimately would approve an action, this did not go back to the meeting to say that it was approved, but the next day there would be a briefing about how this was referred -- how this was being implemented?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they would report back on the implementation.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Therefore, between yesterday and today and on the basis of the question you heard, has your opinion and your position in any way changed with regard to these four civilians not having interfered into the matters of the army?

utterances.speaker: MILAN DJAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not interfere with these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: That was all. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, irony often doesn't travel well in translation. If you look at line -- page 21, line 7, is that an ironic reference to General Sainovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't say General Sainovic. That was an error. I said Nikola Sainovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't hear General Sainovic being interpreted back to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I stated Nikola Sainovic. I don't know how it became General.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters apologise. Perhaps we misheard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would not agree with my colleague Zecevic, who corrected the transcript, because it's page 19, lines 8 and 9, when, or rather, my colleague Zecevic is right in saying that it should have stated a secret name for plans, but the witness also said Grom and the ones that were made before, not later. Can the tape please be double-checked. We disagree amongst ourselves, not all of us have heard the same, but I believe I heard the witness say that and that's why I would kindly request that the tape be double-checked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Remind me of the page and line number. Mr. Bakrac, it was page 6, was it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Colleague Zecevic intervened --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We shall ask CLSS to revise the translation of page 6, lines 23 to 25, the word -- just the first three words of line 25. It's -- would probably be ideal if everyone had an opportunity to see what General Djakovic wrote out last night before he leaves here. So Mr. Haider can photocopy what was written out and just in case there's anything there that ought to be put to him. It won't take you long to read it. The exercise we did the other day in identifying outstanding matters has not -- has met with mixed results and needs to be revisited, and I'm going to do that just now, and then we'll adjourn to enable certain matters to be clarified and to allow counsel to read the parts of the notes written out by General Djakovic. For the moment, that completes your evidence, Mr. Djakovic, but we would like you not to leave just at this stage until everyone has checked what you wrote out last night to see if they want to ask briefly any further questions. While we are dealing with that, looking at what you wrote and reviewing certain other matters, you'll be given access to the Kosovo atlas so that you can see if you can clarify any of the place names. So Mr. Haider will arrange for that to be done. If it turns out that no further questions are necessary, then that will bring to an end the requirement that you're here. And in case you're not back in court, I thank you now for coming here to assist the Tribunal with its inquiry. Please leave the courtroom with the usher and we'll deal with outstanding matters as quickly as possible and let you know whether you can leave as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Since at this point in time that is likely -- that is all the evidence that's available for the Tribunal's consideration, subject to various things I'm going to deal with. We should try today to clear the decks of as many outstanding issues as possible, and on Friday I listed a number. Some have been attended to, a number have not, and the ones I'm now going to deal with include the outstanding ones from Friday plus others which were not raised at that stage. When we adjourn, we will expect work to be done on this so that at some stage today, sooner rather than later, as many of these as possible can be removed from the agenda. Now, a number of them relate to items which have been uploaded either to replace other exhibits because of amendment or as English translations to accompany exhibits, and those ones largely await reaction from the Prosecution. It should be possible to deal with the majority of these in the course of this morning. So if you can separately, Mr. Hannis, compile a list of those as I go through them and knowing that we expect a response, that would be helpful. I'm going to deal with these according to the order in which response -- the order of where responsibility lies. So I'll start with those that are there at the initiation of the Prosecution and then proceed through the various accused. Outstanding for the Prosecution, first of all, P2804, that was to be submitted to CLSS for a revised translation due back yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It was due back yesterday, but it's not back yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that's one to be considered and responded to later. Secondly, the identity documents of the witness Sadiku. You have a motion, Mr. Hannis, to admit P3141 and the Lukic Defence seek the admission of 6D1666. It seems reasonable that if your exhibit's to be admitted that theirs should also. The outstanding issue relates to the translation of P3141. Has it been translated?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It has, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that translation needs to be uploaded. It doesn't appear to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We'll check on that, Your Honour. We thought it was, but it's not showing up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Subject to that, both of these can be admitted, but we'll need to have that confirmed by you later. Milutinovic Defence, Mr. O'Sullivan, any additional information that you could provide on these two exhibits, the order P984 and IC133, the Law of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: That's being filed today, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It has been or will be?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It will be. In the next few minutes it should be filed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you make four courtesy copies or five and let us have them for our break?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, the Sainovic Defence, the revised expert report has been uploaded to e-court. Mr. Hannis, are you able to clarify your position on that or do you wish to take it under advisement?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I take it under advisement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I take it under advisement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. 2D346, the Federal Government Rules of Procedure. A complete version has now been uploaded. Again, that's in your hands, Mr. Hannis. The Pavkovic Defence, the submission on 6D1619, a translation has been provided of that and the document was used with the current witness in court yesterday, so it has been admitted and there will be no further written order, Mr. Lukic -- sorry, Mr. Ackerman. That's 6D1619. Mr. Ackerman, the corrections to the OTP interview of General Pavkovic, what is the situation?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I have no knowledge at all about that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Aleksic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm at a complete loss.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- batted it your way on Friday in court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [In English] Not me. [Interpretation] Mr. Hannis said that he communicated with --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Mr. Ackerman and I can talk during the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: We'll try that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The Lazarevic Defence now. The motion for admission of documents from the bar table filed on the 19th of May, that's on Monday, will be determined in due course. The Prosecution should respond to that by Friday of this week. Now, there are 76 documents, I appreciate it's a large number, but it looks as though you may have time on your hands. Another of these where we -- well, where the response of the Prosecution is awaited in relation to translation is 5D1114 and also -- sorry, yes, 5D1428 and 5D1459. Now, the Lukic Defence, the videos used with the witness Zlatkovic have been re-disclosed as ordered. Now, have you received these, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, we have. I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, one can be dealt with. The new versions of 6D295 and 6D1633 will be admitted in substitution for the existing versions. 6D347, exhibit used with the witness Debeljkovic, English translation, so that's another one for you, Mr. Hannis. 6D5 -- sorry, 6D356, 6D353, 6D344, 6D345, 6D604, 6D1251, these all require your response in relation to translations, Mr. Hannis. The Lukic witness statement -- sorry, that's confusing. The witness statements that had been altered, these were advised to the Trial Chamber by e-mail, Mr. Ivetic, and that was satisfactory for our initial purposes. But they do need to be uploaded into e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That will be done today. That's in the process of being done -- it is actually done actually. They are already in the system, I just don't know if they have been released -- they have been released as well. So that should already be in the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Haider, could you check 6D1631, is that available? Well, in that event, we will admit these revised versions as ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the position with the original statements, Mr. Ivetic? Are these the identical numbers or are these being given new numbers?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Those are the same numbers that these statements had originally. The only difference was that, I believe, the translations -- the English translations of the original Serbian statements were being replaced by the CLSS officials, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Where the full translation is CLSS as opposed to partially CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis, is there a reason for keeping two English versions on -- in relation to these documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Not that I can think of at the moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, they were the ones that were troubling you because of the fact that CLSS had done the translation initially but then there had been amendments to the statements and the Lukic Defence arranged for other translations of the parts which were amended.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, and do you know what's troubling me was not knowing which parts were which --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you were also troubled by the question whether there might be further evidence required from any of these witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I haven't looked at the new ones yet to see if there's any difference that would raise that issue. I doubt that there is, but I need a little time to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, what we shall do is admit these new English translations as additional parts of these exhibits, and they are 6D1631, 1492, 1530, 1533, 1606, and 1614. Mr. Lukic, bar table matters not yet submitted, are there many?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is that in reference to the Rule 70 materials? We're waiting for the Rule 70 provider, that's four documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And that's all?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, everything else, I believe, is in our motion and has been submitted for translation or is in the process of being translated for those that were not translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If we were to determine a final date for the submission of all exhibits from the bar table for your defence case and all translations and make that a week on Friday, the 30th of May, you will make it, will you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I can't speak for the translations, Your Honour. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you know how many there are; I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: There are a significant number. We can only say we can try to get as much done by that date as possible if that's the date that Your Honour submits. We -- as -- we work -- as you can see we work as many hours as we can to get those done, but translations are not a matter that I have much influence over.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you do.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I have some, some.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've got some, indeed. A great deal in fact we would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, for full disclosure, I should say for full answer to your question we do have the one document that Your Honours have been interested in that we just received from the government authorities of Serbia, 6D1667, that one has been translated and is being uploaded. So when I say the only thing remaining outstanding on bar table is Rule 70, that includes that this one has been completed and will be in the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the dead-line, Mr. Ivetic, for any further bar table motions will be the 30th of May and the dead-line for the submission of all translations will be the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And for the record, line 30 -- paragraph -- page 30, line 21, the exhibit in question was 6D1667, I see that didn't make it into the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And as I'm on my feet, there was one other -- in your list of outstanding requests for documents that had been MFI'd to be introduced there was one that we have that wasn't on your list, 6D1489, a request was filed on the 29th of April in that matter, Your Honours, so I don't know whether that's already been dealt with or not but it was absent in the list that you recited to Mr. Hannis a while ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I will check that. Mr. Hannis, you could perhaps look and see if that is another that you can respond to. Now, the interview of General Lukic with the OTP, there is outstanding a motion and it will be dealt with shortly. I had expected it to be done by today but for various reasons it has not been possible. But that doesn't alter the fact that there may be corrections. Now, have you been discussing corrections?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It was my understanding that we had marked items for retranslation along with the Sainovic Defence and had -- I believe that had been submitted some time ago. I'm not positive about that, but I believe it had been submitted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: To the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, we received those from the Lukic Defence the same time we received the ones that Mr. Fila sent us, and that has all gone to CLSS. And you will recall --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What do Mr. Fila's relate to, sorry, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: He selected certain portions of the Lukic interview that he had concerns about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you will recall CLSS for some follow-up guidance on what we wanted them to do, and that was provided to them and I'm not sure what the status is but it is with CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. One further translation issue, Mr. Ivetic, 6D1667 used during the examination of Dujkovic. I think you've obtained a MUP dispatch that was to explain the communications system.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, a courtesy copy of the translations has been sent. This is the document I made reference to earlier that has a translation and is in the process of being uploaded and released into e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Ah, sorry, I should have picked that up. So that's another one for Mr. Hannis to deal with but he won't be in a position to do that today? Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't want to speak for Mr. Hannis, but I presume he probably may not be in a position to deal with it until later today or tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. It looks like you're the man with the answers to provide, Mr. Hannis, and that Mr. Ackerman has the obligation of a discussion with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What we propose is adjourning for an hour. Is that going to be enough, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour. I'll do my best during that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you want to communicate informally, if it's proving difficult, and we might extend that time without assembling the court for that purpose. But let's see what can be achieved first of all and we'll adjourn for the moment until 11.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: First of all, does anyone wish to ask any further questions of Mr. Djakovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There being no one wishing to do that, he can now be discharged. Immediately this hearing finishes the further information he's added will be distributed to everyone, it includes certain annotations trying to clarify certain matters that he's written and further information about localities. Now, I'll go through the outstanding matters, Mr. Hannis, that we should be able to dispose of. P2804.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, as indicated, I'm advised that that will be completed by the close of business today, and we would ask permission to upload it once it's received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where requests are made for translations to be admitted as in these circumstances, parties should understand as a matter of practice from now on that unless they indicate within 24 hours any challenge, the Tribunal will -- the Chamber will proceed to pronounce an order dealing with the item. The identity document, Mr. Hannis, which is P314 -- sorry, I should have completed that by saying, yes, you make your submission as soon as possible. The identity document, P3141.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it has been uploaded and released and attached, and we don't have any objection to the admission of 6D1666, as it seems to pertain and it would be fair to have it admitted as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, on that issue I know that we did not reply or I guess it was a response or reply indicated that there was the one issue with the translation of one of those pages of the documents that had some text that wasn't on the Serbian. I don't know if that's in the version that's been uploaded or not since I haven't been able to see it yet, my computer is still going there. But that was raised in our filing so I hope that that's been addressed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's P3141?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sadije Sadiku, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure what the issue was with the translation and I can't tell you whether or not --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It could be easily verified. The issue was on the birth certificate it said on the top Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and in the translation in the Serbian it doesn't exist because it was taken out after the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The whole purpose of resubmitting this to CLSS was because there was allegedly information in the translation that was not in the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So we will admit P3141 and 6D1666. Then the courtesy copy given to us by Mr. O'Sullivan in respect of his filing on the Law of the Army of Yugoslavia and the passage with either two or three paragraphs, we've had time to consider that. Mr. Hannis, is there any reason why we should not admit IC -- 1C -- sorry, IC133?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well, that will be admitted, Mr. O'Sullivan. That matter's now resolved. There are then two Sainovic documents where we await your reaction, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection to either of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We shall admit 2D393 and 2D346. Corrections to the Pavkovic interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it had been brought to our attention I think by the Chamber actually through a Legal Officer that there was apparently one mistake. I've spoken with Mr. Ackerman. He has no additional ones. I noted what seemed to be one additional one on that same page. So we propose to submit that page, I think it's page 109 in e-court, of Exhibit P948, and we requested to have a translation of that page back by this Friday. And we would then seek to substitute that page into e-court or attach it, whichever's the most logistically appropriate procedure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Probably substitute it. Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. We will order that that filing should be submitted by Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could just intervene, I have finally opened the document, P3141, the error in translation remains in the translation that is in e-court. It says Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, whereas the Serbian does not have that information, and the seal is different, it's of a different state.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We will reconsider the decision I made a moment ago and revoke the order admitting P3141. We have Mr. Hannis's submission on that, and Mr. Ivetic will respond hopefully within 24 hours. And unless between the two of you it can be sorted out quicker than that and we'll just have to pronounce a written order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm willing to resubmit it to CLSS to revise that because I think Mr. Ivetic is correct from what I can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the resubmission can't have made clear what was required, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm willing to do what's most expeditious --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, please do it, it will be necessary, in which case we will leave it to you to make the appropriate filing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But we'll order you to do that by Friday.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. We will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There were then certain Lazarevic documents awaiting your reaction, 5D1114 and 1428 and 1459.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection to any of those three.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. They will be admitted. Then turning to the Lukic case, 6D347.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That will be admitted. And then there's a series, 356, 353, 344, and 345.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: These will be admitted. Then 6D604 and 6D1251.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: 604, as I understand the application, was for certain pages from that entire document, and as proposed no objection. And no objection to 1251.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's 38 pages, and therefore both that and 1251 will be admitted. Now, I understand that the corrections in the Lukic interview have been translated. Has that translation been uploaded, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Oh, yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: -- in the process as I understand it, Your Honour. And I guess a word of explanation. It appears that CLSS made their entries in red on the document, so where there is the English, for example, Investigator Curtis asked questions in English, then there is a B/C/S translation by the interpreter on site during the interview, and CLSS in some of those places where there was an issue has put what the B/C/S says and you'll see there might be some slight variation in that English translation from what the original English was for whatever argument there is to be made from it. From my view, it doesn't appear to be serious differences, but it's not exactly word for word.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you intend to make a filing in response then? It's the Lukic Defence that have uploaded this I think -- are we at cross-purposes here? We're talking about 6D1667.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm talking about something else, Your Honour. I thought you were talking about the Lukic interview.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Sorry, let's go to the interview then in that case. In relation to the interview, you should have received now an English -- a translation of the parts that were to be corrected; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you better repeat -- since I was thinking about something else you better repeat what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It's in the process of being uploaded and what changes or what additions CLSS made in the transcript in the highlighted portions that we requested them to look at are in red ink. Everything else is in black so you can see what CLSS has done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Ivetic, is there any objections from your point of view to the admission of this translation?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, we filed an objection for other reasons. I haven't seen these. I would have to look through them to see what -- and I assume if they're translated they're translated so that shouldn't be an issue. But I haven't seen the translations as yet because it was sent by the OTP so we don't have a -- and CLSS can't give us copies and you have to get --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Since we are to deal with the question of the interview, it would be necessary for you to make any filing you want to make about the translation question separately but within 24 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 24 hours. Thank you, Your Honour, we will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Petrovic, this affects you, I think, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we did, indeed, raise those objections in terms of the content of the transcript, while it wasn't clear that the content of this interview would not directly relate to our client. Since this question was resolved ultimately through your decision, we accept any procedure that the Lukic Defence and the Prosecutor agree on. We waive our objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, there will be a written order dealing with this interview and it will deal with the question of the translation at the same time. That -- there's then 6D1667, now that's a translation which has been uploaded, Mr. Hannis, but have you had time to see this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have, Your Honour, and we have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. 6D1667 translation will be admitted. You raised as an omission from the list, Mr. Ivetic, 6D1489. In fact, that is a document on your bar table motion, and until the bar table motion is dealt with the translation can't really be dealt with.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine then in that case, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are there any other procedural issues parties wish us to address?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think there was the issue regarding the revised versions of the Lukic witness statements, and I have no objection to those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think I already said that these were admitted, and the outstanding question was whether to substitute them for the existing exhibit or whether both should remain and for the moment it was both. Now, if you're satisfied they can be substituted then that progresses matters because that will have to be resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm satisfied with them being substituted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, that will happen in the case of each of these exhibits, and they are 6D1631, 1492, 1530, 1533, 1606, and 1614. Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I raise two questions with Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: One, you indicated that from now on the general rule regarding these translations would be if there was no objection from a party within 24 hours then they would be allowed in. I know there's -- you set a dead-line for the 30th of May for the Defence -- for Lukic Defence regarding their outstanding translations. I don't know how many there are. I think there's still a substantial number. The 30th of May falls on a Friday and depending on how many there are I would like to have additional time so I don't have to work 24 hours on Saturday to try and respond. Maybe I'll have no objections, but I just don't know. So I would request now some dead-line beyond 24 hours for those particular items.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: For the ones that arrive on the 30th?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Well, for any that arrive on the 30th, we will allow you until the Wednesday to deal with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Should there be a situation where additional time is required, then you know that you should apply to us, but that application should be made within 24 hours of receiving the document unless it falls on the 30th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I understand. I see Mr. Ackerman on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, there's an ancillary issue that may cause confusion and that is the untranslated documents that are listed in the Lukic bar table motion. I trust those are not affected by the May 30th dead-line issue, I don't know, because they haven't even been dealt with with regard to admission yet. But we had both -- Mr. Hannis and I both requested in our objections that we be given additional time to deal with those that have not yet been translated in terms of objecting to the bar table. So I don't know how you want to handle that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, the 30th of May is the dead-line for the translations, and we will separately deal with the issue that you raise on the understanding that the English versions will be there by the 30th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The last thing, Your Honour, was a logistical question regarding the additions that General Djakovic now has made by writing out --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I'm not sure how we should put those into e-court in connection with P1468 because we have made a number of references to the pre-existing page numbers without the newly identified illegible portions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That will be dealt with in the way I indicated earlier, which is by a joint filing by all parties. So it is for you to reach agreement on what you do. It would probably be best to keep what he has written separate -- as a separate document but part of that exhibit; however, if it emerges from your consideration of the whole issue that the revisal should be incorporated into one complete version of 1468, including his revisals, then you would make an appropriate filing and we would consider it. But you rightly point out the difficulty associated with that in respect that references have been made to the document a number of times. However, you could probably satisfy yourself whether that is a difficulty and decide what's the best way to do it. We are asking CLSS to deal with this as a matter of urgency, and I envisage this being done this week and the parties being in a position to make this filing at the beginning of next week at the latest but hopefully by the end of this week. Mr. Haider will deal with it immediately we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Haider is suggesting that we give an IC number to the handwritten version provided by Mr. Djakovic. I think we should do that and we will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So since that includes the place names that he was clarifying then, if we give that one document an IC number for the moment it will be on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be IC199, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. As the parties here are aware but as is not yet publicly known, the Trial Chamber has endeavoured to secure the attendance of certain Chamber witnesses in addition to Mr. Djakovic. The Chamber has been unable to secure the attendance of Christopher Hill, Boris Majorski and Aleksandar Dimitrijevic. We will therefore adjourn now until the 22nd of July at 11.00 a.m., when we will hear closing arguments. We hope to have the rest of the 22nd of July available to us and we hope to have the following three full days, but that remains to be determined. The precise allocation we can secure cannot be clarified to us at this moment. We are confident there will be adequate time during these four days leading to the final day of this term, that's the 25th, for the closing arguments of the parties, that's almost nine weeks from now. In the meantime, final briefs are due on the 8th of July but the Chamber would be greatly assisted by the earlier production of these briefs if any party finds it possible to do that. So we now adjourn until the 22nd of July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 22nd day of July, 2008, at 11.00 a.m. 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 12.30 p.m.,
